title: [YSQL] Regression in local time spent in queries with large IN clause
body: Jira Link: [DB-8134](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-8134) ### Description The latency on queries of the form `SELECT * FROM t WHERE a IN (1, ... 10000)` has doubled since D27507 / ddf6d0b910f9f9c291766108c09fc91b3162e267. It's not as noticeable because the commit landed shortly after the large regression introduced by D27262 was fixed (D27679), and it only impacts colocated tables. If you look closely at the perf graph, you can see that the 1000row case has slightly increased since before the spike. ## Testing ## I used the schema: ```sql CREATE TABLE t (a int PRIMARY KEY, b INT, c INT); INSERT INTO t SELECT g, g, g FROM generate_series(1, 10000) g; CREATE INDEX ON t (b); ``` I used the following test script to execute a PREPARED query 500x, with a specified number of IN values: (usage: `python3 local-runner.py 1000` will run a query with `1, 2, 3, ..., 999, 1000` in the IN clause). ```python import sys import subprocess import statistics import time n = int(sys.argv[1]) + 1 in_file = "in.sql" out_file = "out.txt" runs = 500 with open(in_file, "w+") as f: f.write(f"\\c col;\n") f.write(f"PREPARE s AS SELECT * FROM t WHERE b IN ({','.join(str(i) for i in range(1, n))});\n") for i in range(0, runs): f.write(f"EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, DIST) EXECUTE s;\n") subprocess.run(["./bin/ysqlsh", "-f", "in.sql", "-o", "out.txt"]) exec_time = [] storage_time = [] with open(out_file, "r") as f: for line in f: if line.startswith(" Execution Time:"): exec_time += [float(line.split(": ")[1].split(" ")[0])] if line.startswith(" Storage Execution Time: "): storage_time += [float(line.split(": ")[1].split(" ")[0])] if (exec_time): print(statistics.median(exec_time)) if (storage_time): print(statistics.median(storage_time)) ``` I slightly modified the file each time to collect variations of `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a IN...`, `SELECT * FROM t WHERE a IN...`, `SELECT * FROM t WHERE b IN...`, and `SELECT b FROM t WHERE b IN...`. ### Results ### These numbers are produced using a PREPARED query and using the median of 500 runs. However, they were run on my devserver for simplicity of identifying the failing commit. No significant change on the non-colocated, 10000row case. Our perf service also does not show a change in the non-colocated case for up to 1000rows. 60% regression on the colocated, 1000row case when we select all columns. Our perf service shows a slight increase in the 1000row case after this commit landed (2.19.3.0-b6), but only tests `SELECT pkey FROM t WHERE pkey IN (...)`. (does not test `SELECT * FROM ...` or `SELECT pkey, b, c FROM ...` 125% regression on the colocated, 10000row case when we select all columns. Our perf service does not test 10000row selection. ### Warning: Please confirm that this issue does not contain any sensitive information - [X] I confirm this issue does not contain any sensitive information.
